title: Ambiguous Multiline Endline Comment
pattern: An endline comment placed on the opening line of a control block, intended to describe the entire block.
why_bad: Scope ambiguity. It is visually unclear whether the comment refers solely to the first line (the loop initialization) or the entire block body, forcing readers to parse both in detail.
detection: Endline comments placed on `for`, `while`, `match`, or `if` headers describing the action of subsequent statements.
counterexample: A block comment placed on its own line above the loop, unambiguously scoping the description to the whole block.
fix: Move the comment to a separate block comment above the control loop to clearly signal its scope.
source: Steve McConnell, *Code Complete* (2004), Chapter 32 ("Endline Comments and Their Problems - Avoid endline comments for multiple lines of code").
